nodes.title: Pine Tree Trail Lodge
nodes.summary: A spacious family oasis in central Maine. Step into the vibrant Game Room & Karaoke Lounge, where unforgettable memories await — a neon-lit karaoke stage with a microphone ready for your star performance, a retro arcade, foosball, a candy crane machine, and a pool. Even when the weather is bad, the family is never sad. It's the perfect base for multi-generational getaways and birthday celebrations.

nodes.title: Grand luxury meets nonstop fun — Game Room, Karaoke, Pool & more
nodes.summary: Lively yet cozy and made for family vacations. Book the entire lodge for your group and enjoy the Game Room & Karaoke Lounge, a retro arcade, foosball, a candy crane machine, and the pool.

nodes.title: Pine Tree Trail Lodge Radio
nodes.summary: Broadcasting from a converted tack room at the edge of the pines, Pine Tree Trail Lodge Radio is a listener-supported country, roots, and Americana station. We play the songs that sound like the trail at dusk — steel guitar, close harmony, and a story in every verse. No algorithms and no auto-DJ after dark: just people who love this music picking the next record. Whether you're stoking the woodstove at the lodge or driving the county road home, we're the sound of the pines.

nodes.title: A roots & Americana format
nodes.summary: Our sound sits where classic country meets folk, bluegrass, and singer-songwriter roots — Americana in the truest sense. Expect Telecasters and fiddles, murder ballads and honky-tonk, brand-new voices right alongside the records that built the genre.

nodes.title: Country, the way it was meant to sound
nodes.summary: We lean into traditional and outlaw country — the twang, the heartbreak, the Bakersfield shuffle — and skip the studio gloss. If it has a pedal steel and it means every word, it belongs on this station.

nodes.title: Front-porch roots music
nodes.summary: Bluegrass, old-time string bands, gospel harmony, and the folk tradition that runs underneath it all. This is music made to be played on a porch, and we treat it that way.

nodes.title: Trailhead Mornings
nodes.summary: Ease into the day with warm acoustic sets, a weather-and-trail report, and the occasional live in-studio song. Hosted with a full pot of coffee and no hurry at all.

nodes.title: The Honky-Tonk Hour
nodes.summary: One hour, all twang. Classic and outlaw country from the jukebox era — the barroom weepers, the shuffle beats, and the songs that made the neon glow.

nodes.title: Front Porch Sessions
nodes.summary: Bluegrass, old-time, and string-band music recorded live around a single microphone — the way it's played on the porch after supper, mistakes and all.

nodes.title: New Roots Radio
nodes.summary: The next generation of Americana — emerging songwriters, debut records, and the artists we're betting you'll be hearing everywhere a year from now.

nodes.title: Night Drive
nodes.summary: After dark it slows down: dusty ballads, pedal steel, and long instrumental stretches for the quiet drive home through the pines.

nodes.title: Weekdays
nodes.summary: 6–10a Trailhead Mornings · 10a–12p Open Range (staff picks) · 12–1p The Honky-Tonk Hour · 1–6p Afternoon Drift · 6–8p New Roots Radio · 8p–12a Night Drive.

nodes.title: Saturdays
nodes.summary: 8–11a Front Porch Sessions · 11a–2p Bluegrass Brunch · 2–6p the Saturday Roundup request show · 6–9p Barn Dance (two-step and western swing) · 9p–1a Night Drive.

nodes.title: Sundays
nodes.summary: 9a–12p Gospel & Grass (sacred harp, spirituals, and gospel bluegrass) · 12–4p the Sunday Songbook · 4–7p Storytellers, songwriters in their own words · 7–11p Night Drive.

nodes.title: Artist in rotation: Gillian Welch & David Rawlings
nodes.summary: Spare, haunting Appalachian-inflected duets that helped define modern Americana. A cornerstone of our afternoon and late-night sets.

nodes.title: Artist in rotation: Emmylou Harris
nodes.summary: A voice that bridges country, folk, and rock — from the Gram Parsons years to Wrecking Ball and beyond. Always welcome on this frequency.

nodes.title: Artist in rotation: Sturgill Simpson
nodes.summary: Outlaw grit meets restless experimentation. We spin the barn-burners on the Honky-Tonk Hour and the slow ones after midnight.

nodes.title: "Wagon Wheel" — Old Crow Medicine Show
nodes.summary: A modern string-band anthem built on a Bob Dylan sketch. A perennial request-line favorite on the Saturday Roundup.

nodes.title: "Angel from Montgomery" — John Prine
nodes.summary: One of the great American songs — plainspoken, aching, and perfect. We play both Prine's version and Bonnie Raitt's.

nodes.title: "Wayfaring Stranger" — traditional
nodes.summary: A traditional folk spiritual that turns up on Night Drive and Gospel & Grass alike. Every generation records it, and we play the best of them.

nodes.title: Marla Reyes — Trailhead Mornings
nodes.summary: Marla grew up on her grandfather's bluegrass records and has been on the air for fifteen years. She opens the station most mornings with whatever song she couldn't stop humming on the drive up the trail.

nodes.title: Cal Doyle — The Honky-Tonk Hour & Night Drive
nodes.summary: A former touring pedal-steel player, Cal knows every B-side and the story behind it. His late-night sets wander from Bakersfield to the back roads and rarely take the obvious turn.

nodes.title: The Front Porch Collective
nodes.summary: Front Porch Sessions is hosted by a rotating circle of local pickers who record the show live around one microphone. Different players most weeks — same porch, same welcome.

nodes.title: How can I listen?
nodes.summary: A live stream is on the way — until then you can browse the schedule and shows here. When we go live, you'll be able to tune in right from this page.

nodes.title: Can I request a song?
nodes.summary: Yes — the Saturday Roundup and Sunday Songbook are built around listener requests. Send them our way and we'll do our best to work them into the set.

nodes.title: I'm an artist — how do I get played?
nodes.summary: New Roots Radio exists to spotlight emerging Americana and roots artists. Reach out with a link to your music; we listen to everything that comes in.
